[{"claim": "Conservative individuals are more likely to receive booster doses in liberal regions.", "quotes": [{"text": "Most strikingly, for booster status the interaction between political orientation and political climate indicated that the most liberal participants were over 65% likely to get boosted regardless of climate. The most conservative participants in liberal climates were 60% likely to get boosted, while conservatives in conservative climates were less than 35% likely to get boosted (OR =.83, p = .026).", "page": 8}]}]

[{"claim": "The study used online survey data from 683 U.S. participants collected between March 8 and April 19, 2023.", "quotes": [{"text": "We collected online survey data from 683 participants between March 8 and April 19, 2023.", "page": 1}]}, {"claim": "Participants self-reported their political conservatism, regional political climate, vaccine status, booster status, and vaccine hesitancy.", "quotes": [{"text": "The online survey assessed demographic control variables (i.e., age, gender, race, income, education, perceived vaccine access), predictor variables (i.e., political conservatism, regional political climate) and outcome variables (i.e., vaccine status, booster status, vaccine hesitancy, booster hesitancy).", "page": 3}]}, {"claim": "Regional political climate was measured by the percentage of Republican votes in the 2020 presidential election for each participant's zip code.", "quotes": [{"text": "We used the % Republican vote by zip code as a measure of conservative regional climate.", "page": 4}]}, {"claim": "Vaccine hesitancy was measured using seven items from the Attitudes towards Adult Vaccination Scale, modified to assess attitudes toward the COVID-19 vaccine.", "quotes": [{"text": "Vaccine hesitancy (i.e., negative attitudes toward vaccination) was measured using the seven items from the Attitudes towards Adult Vaccination Scale [24], which assesses the perceived value of vaccines in general. [{"claim": "Conservatives in liberal political climates were less vaccine hesitant than their conservative counterparts in conservative regions.", "quotes": [{"text": "However, conservatives living in liberal political climates were less vaccine hesitant than their conservative counterparts living in conservative regions.", "page": 1}]}, {"claim": "The likelihood of receiving a COVID-19 booster was significantly associated with both political conservatism and conservative regional climate, with a significant interaction effect.", "quotes": [{"text": "A similar interaction was for the likelihood of receiving a COVID-19 booster (OR =.84, p = .049).", "page": 1}]}, {"claim": "The most politically liberal individuals were over 65% likely to get a booster regardless of regional climate.", "quotes": [{"text": "The most liberal participants were over 65% likely to get boosted regardless of climate.", "page": 8}]}, {"claim": "For booster status, the interaction between political orientation and political climate showed that conservative individuals in liberal climates were more likely to receive boosters than in conservative climates.", "quotes": [{"text": "The most conservative participants in liberal climates were 60% likely to get boosted, while conservatives in conservative climates were less than 35% likely to get boosted (OR =.83, p = .026).", "page": 8}]}, {"claim": "The interaction between political conservatism and conservative regional climate was significant for booster hesitancy and booster status, but not for vaccine status.", "quotes": [{"text": "The interaction for vaccination was not significant, this difference between attitudes (hesitancy) and action (vaccination), likely reflects the high prevalence of COVID-19 vaccine mandates.", "page": 10}]}]
